12:00 Local Time, 07:00 GMT, 12:30 IST: What is a safe total in ODIs these days? We've seen 400+ totals chased down twice in the last month, one of them in this very tri-series. England, powered by Harry Brook's record-breaking double century, piled up 429, only for Sri Lanka to pull off a stunning chase with a ball to spare. So, what can we expect today? Hello and welcome to match four of the tri-series.. Would England have recovered from that heartbreak? They'll need to, because they're the only team without a win so far, and another defeat would dent their chances of making the final. Standing in their way are a Pakistan side flying high with two wins from two. Victory today would not only extend their unbeaten run but also seal their place in the final.

England's biggest concern has been their bowling. They've conceded 302 and 429 in their two outings, and the changes made ahead of the second game did little to improve matters. Adil Rashid was among those left out in favour of Liam Dawson, but the experienced leg-spinner could return to provide a wrist-spin option on these flat surfaces. The pace attack, relatively inexperienced, hasn't had much assistance from the pitches either. They'll need to find a way to contain Pakistan, because the batting has largely done its job. The openers have provided starts in both games, Brook is coming off that historic double ton, and the middle order has chipped in as well.

Pakistan, meanwhile, have had their own concerns at the top. Their top order has struggled in both games, but the middle order has stepped up to bail them out and push them past 300 on both occasions. Their bowlers, led by skipper Shaheen Afridi, have then done enough to defend those totals. Salman Agha struck a century in the opening game, while Arafat Minhas has made valuable contributions with both bat and ball. Home conditions have certainly helped and Pakistan will be keen to make it three wins out of three and book their place in the final. Can England bounce back, or will Pakistan continue their winning run? The toss and team news are coming up. Stay tuned!
Pakistan have won the toss and have opted to field

Shaheen Afridi: We will bowl first. [On whether the decision was influenced by the fresh surface] Yeah, I think it's a new surface and we also include one extra spinner, so I hope it will (work). [On whether being one win away from securing a place in the final adds confidence or pressure] Look, I feel every day is a different day, so we just like to focus on our good things and continue that, and I hope our bowlers play the big role again. [On addressing concerns about the top order] Not too much talk, just for the good things we address, like how we play our best cricket and how can we improve in the next games. That's it, nothing more. [On team changes] Two changes: Shadab in and Faheem rested. Unfortunately Naseem had an injury in the warm-up, he had a left hand two finger dislocated. So he will be fine for the next game, but we give him rest to, like we need the next two games more important for us. Razaullah makes his debut.

Harry Brook: It looks like a good wicket. We were going to have a bat, so yeah we're pretty pleased with that. [On his fitness and recovery] Yeah, always good, always fit and raring to go. [On addressing England's bowling concerns after conceding 429 against Sri Lanka] Just chatting really. We know what the conditions present, we know we've got to try and be a little bit more consistent with and around the top of the stumps. So yeah, we have a lot of clarity going into this game with that. [On team changes] Henry Crocombe comes in to make his debut, Josh Tongue is out.

Pitch Report | Aamer Sohail: "If Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium was a high-scoring venue, Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore is not far behind. The only exception at times here is it offers something for the spinners. Other than that, we have seen plenty of 300-plus runs here. So let's see how this pitch is being curated for this game. If you knock it, it gives you that 'tot' sound. It has a grass covering and I'm afraid spinners might not get that help, which we were alluding to. Nice grass covering. This pitch will offer consistent pace and bounce and batting will be very easy. The batters can express themselves."
